title: Find why the Engram control process ended mid-request at 13:25Z, so TermAl named-root calls never see EOF before a reply
outcome: Find why the Engram control process ended mid-request at 13:25Z, so TermAl named-root calls never see EOF before a reply
acceptance: The 2026-11-02 13:25Z exit cause is classified as not recoverable from retained evidence, with ruled-out candidates named, and added diagnostics make the next occurrence attributable.

When the Engram control process is interrupted with a request in flight, Engram's side is defined and tested: an unwind writes a durable correlated diagnostic and exits with a fixed code; an ordinary transport I/O failure ends only the current serve, and an exact retry on a fresh connection returns the original result without a duplicate write. The parent-side mapping of a child exit or reap to a defined caller error is TermAl's, tracked in TermAl w-eef208cb36ae.
Engram's control process leaves a durable diagnostic for an abnormal exit, so the next occurrence can be diagnosed from the store home
